spec_cite: docs/wire-protocol-v2/pairing.md §6.3 (canonical form: count(u8) || id(u32 BE) ascending)
description: A well-formed but unknown capability id is IGNORED, not rejected: the canonical single-id list [7] is accepted and the honored intersection echoed back is empty.
preconditions: Session authenticated; state NEGOTIATING (request_id 2 follows the auth exchange's 1).
v2.0 assigns no capability ids, so id 7 is unknown-but-optional; spec §4.5 rules unknown ids ignored.
The list on the wire is unique and ascending, so the canonical encoding exists: 01 00000007.
assertions: The Negotiate is well-formed (single id, ascending, unique) — no 401.
Id 7 is unknown in v2.0 (no ids are assigned); per spec §4.5 it is ignored and the honored intersection is empty: NegotiateResponse.capabilities = [] (not encoded).
102 (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY) is reserved for a KNOWN capability the Server cannot honor — unreachable in v2.0 because no ids exist yet; only a reviewed spec revision can assign one (spec §4.5).
